last_transition_reason: The proof correctly derives the stated identity for E_n(a/n) by rewriting floor(ka/n) via the quotient-remainder decomposition ak = nq_k + r_k, then summing and using r_n = 0. It matches the lemma sketch exactly, with no semantic drift and no dependency issues.
latest_nl_proof:
Fix an integer n>1 and an integer a with 0<=a<=n-1, and set x=a/n. By the definition of E_n,
E_n(a/n)=\lfloor n(a/n)\rfloor-\sum_{k=1}^n \frac{\lfloor k(a/n)\rfloor}{k}=a-\sum_{k=1}^n \frac{\lfloor ka/n\rfloor}{k}.

For each k in {1,...,n}, let r_k be the least nonnegative residue of ak modulo n; equivalently, 0<=r_k<n and ak\equiv r_k (mod n). Then there exists an integer q_k such that
ak=nq_k+r_k,
and therefore
\lfloor ka/n\rfloor=q_k=\frac{ak-r_k}{n}.
Hence
\sum_{k=1}^n \frac{\lfloor ka/n\rfloor}{k}
=\sum_{k=1}^n \frac{ak-r_k}{nk}
=\sum_{k=1}^n \left(\frac{a}{n}-\frac{r_k}{nk}\right)
=a-\frac1n\sum_{k=1}^n \frac{r_k}{k}.
Substituting this into the formula for E_n(a/n) gives
E_n(a/n)=a-\left(a-\frac1n\sum_{k=1}^n \frac{r_k}{k}\right)=\frac1n\sum_{k=1}^n \frac{r_k}{k}.

Finally, when k=n we have an\equiv 0 (mod n), so r_n=0. Thus the k=n term vanishes, and
E_n(a/n)=\frac1n\sum_{k=1}^{n-1} \frac{r_k}{k}.
Since r_k=Res_n(a,k), this is exactly
E_n(a/n)=\frac1n\sum_{k=1}^{n-1} \frac{Res_n(a,k)}{k}.
role_in_parent: Convert the discrete endpoint value into a weighted sum of least residues modulo n.
statement_nl: For every integer n>1 and every integer a with 0 <= a <= n-1, one has E_n(a/n) = (1/n) * sum_{k=1}^{n-1} Res_n(a,k)/k.

domain_restrictions: n is an integer and n > 1
a is an integer and 0 <= a <= n - 1
the summation index k is an integer with 1 <= k <= n - 1
division by n and division by k are defined (implicitly requiring n != 0 and k != 0, ensured by n > 1 and k >= 1)
statement_semantic_sketch.normalized_claim: For all integers n with n > 1 and for all integers a with 0 <= a <= n - 1, letting x be the rational a divided by n, we have: E_n of x equals (1 divided by n) times the sum over integers k from 1 to n - 1 of Res_n of (a,k) divided by k.

for all integer a with 0 <= a <= n - 1
